newsitem.title: UK: DeBeers to end current Russian diamond pact.
newsitem.headline: DeBeers to end current Russian diamond pact.

text.p: De Beers, still waiting for the Russian government to approve a new diamond sales pact, said on Wednesday it will stop buying Russian diamonds from December 31 under the terms of the agreement currently in place.
That deal officially expired at the end of last year, but remained operational as long as no new pact was agreed.
De Beers -- hopeful a new deal will be concluded in due course -- said it expected to continue buying significant amounts of Russian diamonds.
"De Beers still hopes that the Russian government will ratify the new trade agreement in due course," De Beers said.
"In any event, De Beers intends in the New Year to review its relationship with the relevant Russian authorities," De Beers said in a statement.
The South African company has been in protracted talks with Russia to reach a new agreement to market the country's rough diamonds through De Beers' Central Selling Organisation.
A breakthrough seemed close when De Beers signed a memorandum of understanding with the Russian government in February.

All that was needed then, was a final agreement with Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), Russia's major diamond producer. A deal was reached in September, with both parties waiting since then for approval from the Russian government.
De Beers, meanwhile, continued buying rough diamonds under the old agreement.

"These arrangements have not operated satisfactorily in 1996 and therefore De Beers has indicated to the Russian government and ARS that it is not prepared to continue to buy diamonds under the old agreement beyond December 31, 1996," De Beers said a statement.
CSO director Tim Capon declined to say whether De Beers would start buying fewer Russian diamnonds in 1997 if the new sales pact was still not approved by then.

"Given the fact that this process is dragging on, what we are saying is that we expect to be talking to the Russians about buying from then again in 1997, but we are not prepared to go on on precisely the same basis," Capon told Reuters.
"But I am not going to speculate whether we'll be buying more or less," he said.
De Beers' CSO markets about 75 percent of all the world's rough diamond production. Russia makes up about 20 percent of the total CSO sales.
